headline: Medium risk: shared document workflows can leak data and trigger prompt-injection/cascading errors; no direct evidence of a blocked pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts, and PaddleOCR processes documents/images; that creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if OCR or extracted text is fed back into kotaemon. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into kotaemon without provenance filtering
IF kotaemon treats extracted document text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OCR output into chat prompts
Add a provenance tag to OCR-derived text before display
Review one sample pipeline for instruction-like text handling
Restrict uploads to trusted documents only
requires-engineering: add prompt-injection filtering at the ingestion boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images with allowlisted egress. A shared workspace or handoff could expose sensitive content from A to B or vice versa, but the profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or upload directory
IF OCR inputs include documents containing secrets or chat transcripts
mitigations: Separate input/output folders per agent
Remove secrets from documents before OCR
Limit uploads to non-sensitive samples
Check whether either agent forwards file contents to external APIs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while PaddleOCR exposes API-based processing but no write surface or shared mutable resource is documented. The pair shows possible overlap only if an external orchestrator points both at the same files, so the conflict is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same local directory
IF an orchestrator reuses the same mutable artifacts across runs
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Run only one writer per artifact path
Use read-only mounts for OCR inputs
Check for concurrent writes during a test run
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can surface citations and generated answers, and PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images. If OCR output is fed into kotaemon without verification, downstream answers can inherit OCR mistakes or injected text; the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as authoritative input to kotaemon
IF no human or rule-based verification checks OCR text before retrieval
mitigations: Spot-check OCR output on one document
Require a verification step before indexing
Flag low-confidence OCR spans
Keep source images linked to extracted text
requires-engineering: add validation before downstream actioning

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and chat transcripts, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If regulated or sensitive documents are routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits the documented gap.
conditions: IF regulated documents or chat transcripts are processed by both agents
IF their retention or deletion settings differ for the same data class
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both tools
Exclude regulated data from OCR runs
Document where extracted text is stored
Delete test artifacts after validation
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
